ge.note: Trailing diluted EPS as first filed (no later restatements), restated for splits. Weeks with negative or no recent earnings have no P/E.
ge.source: SEC EDGAR XBRL (diluted EPS, four quarters summed); prices Yahoo Finance weekly closes.

wb.source: Issuers' daily curves (US, DE, UK, JP, CA, AU), live quotes where available, OECD monthly averages elsewhere; policy rates BIS; inflation IMF WEO (this year's estimate); ratings Damodaran.
wb.note: Real yield = 10-year minus the IMF's inflation estimate for this year — a rough guide, not a TIPS-style market real yield. Euro-area members use the ECB rate.

ds.source: SEC EDGAR full text of the latest 10-K (or 20-F/40-F), the last two 10-Qs and the last three 8-Ks with their press releases; ranked by BM25 relevance.

curves.name: United Kingdom
curves.source: Bank of England nominal zero-coupon gilt curve

curves.name: Canada
curves.source: Bank of Canada benchmark bond yields

fwcv.note: Forwards are what today's curve locks in: 5y5y is the 5-year rate five years from now. Yields are treated as zero-coupon rates (exact for the Bundesbank, ECB and Bank of England curves; a close approximation for par curves).
fwcv.source: United States: US Treasury par yield curve; Germany: Deutsche Bundesbank (zero-coupon, Svensson); Euro area AAA: ECB AAA-rated euro-area government curve; United Kingdom: Bank of England nominal zero-coupon gilt curve; Japan: Ministry of Finance JGB curve; Canada: Bank of Canada benchmark bond yields; Australia: Reserve Bank of Australia (table F2)

ecfc.note: IMF forecasts for 2026 and 2027. 'Latest CPI' is the most recent actual year-on-year print (BIS); the gap to the IMF's full-year figure shows whether inflation is running ahead of or behind the forecast. World growth is weighted by GDP in US dollars (the IMF's own headline uses purchasing-power weights).
ecfc.source: IMF World Economic Outlook; CPI and policy rates BIS.

fomc.note: Dots are the median of FOMC participants' year-end projections from the latest Summary of Economic Projections; the market path is the fed funds futures-implied rate after each meeting (WIRP).
fomc.source: FRED (Federal Reserve target range, effective rate, Summary of Economic Projections); CME fed funds futures via Yahoo.

em.name: Apple Inc.
em.source: SEC EDGAR XBRL, as first filed (EPS restated for later splits); Q4 derived as the 10-K year minus the first three quarters where it isn't reported.

ea.name: S&P 500
ea.note: Reports from index members over the last 45 days, against the analysts' consensus Yahoo shows. Reaction is the close before the report to the first close after it (next day for reports after the bell); not adjusted for the market.
ea.source: Yahoo Finance earnings calendar; State Street SPY full daily holdings (weights as held by the ETF); prices from the local daily-bars store (Massive) or Yahoo.

borrow.note: Liquid = over $5M traded on the last session, or a member of the S&P 500 or Nasdaq 100. A fee above ~5% a year usually means heavy short demand or scarce supply.
borrow.source: Interactive Brokers stock-loan file; dollar volume from the local daily-bars store (Massive).

borrowone.name: TESLA INC
borrowone.note: Fee is the annual rate IBKR charges to borrow the shares; rebate is what a short seller earns on the cash (negative when the fee exceeds the benchmark rate). 'Available' is IBKR's own lendable inventory, capped at 10 million in the file.
borrowone.source: Interactive Brokers stock-loan file (public FTP, updated through the day).

dark.note: Off-exchange = dark pools (ATS) plus wholesalers and internalisers (mostly retail orders filled by firms such as Citadel and Virtu). FINRA publishes Tier 1 stocks two weeks after the week ends, others four weeks after. Share is of all shares traded that week (Yahoo consolidated volume).
dark.source: FINRA OTC Transparency (weekly ATS and non-ATS summaries); volume Yahoo Finance.

prob.note: Market-implied (risk-neutral) distribution: it prices in investors' demand for protection, so it tends to put more weight on falls than history would. The lognormal uses the at-the-money volatility only.
prob.source: Yahoo Finance options (15-min delayed). IV solved from the bid/ask mid and Greeks via Black–Scholes–Merton (European approximation for US-style options).; smile fitted on out-of-the-money quotes, Breeden–Litzenberger density.

crpr.name: Microsoft Corporation
crpr.note: Synthetic rating: the rating whose typical interest coverage (operating income ÷ interest, last four quarters) matches this company's — Damodaran's method for large non-financial firms; not an agency rating. Altman Z is the original public-manufacturer model (safe above 2.99, distress below 1.81); Piotroski F scores nine yes/no tests (8–9 strong, 0–2 weak).
crpr.source: SEC EDGAR XBRL; coverage→rating→spread table from Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern); market cap Yahoo; 10-year Treasury yield.

leag.note: Counts companies whose merger proxy, S-4 or tender-offer response contains an 'Opinion of <bank>' section — the bank that gave a fairness opinion to the board. Deal values aren't in the search index, so this ranks by number of deals; both sides of a deal can each count when both are US-listed. Search covers the most recent 100 matching documents per bank.

spf.note: Median of about 35 professional forecasters, surveyed each quarter by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia — the free equivalent of an economist consensus survey. 'Previous' is the last survey's forecast for the same period.
spf.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Survey of Professional Forecasters.

swap.note: Par rates from that day's reported trades: new, spot-starting, outright swaps at whole-year maturities, notional-weighted median of the fixed rate (off-market prints dropped). Swap spread = SOFR swap minus Treasury par yield (negative spreads are normal in USD).
swap.source: DTCC public swap data (CFTC Part 43 real-time reports), internal use; Treasury curve US Treasury.

cdsx.note: IG, iTraxx Main and Crossover trade as spreads (bp); CDX HY and EM trade as prices (100 = par, lower = wider). Levels are the median of that day's reported trades in the most-traded (on-the-run 5-year) maturity. The HY spread is approximate (coupon minus upfront ÷ ~4.3 years of risky duration).
cdsx.source: DTCC public swap data (CFTC Part 43), internal use.

cdsa.note: Counts new single-name CDS trades by reference entity (grouped by the issuer part of the reference bond's ISIN). Notional is capped in the public tape for large trades, so it understates block size. Busy names are where credit protection is being bought or sold — often around earnings, downgrades or M&A.
cdsa.source: DTCC public security-based swap data (SEC Regulation SBSR), internal use; names OpenFIGI.

exth.note: Change is against the previous regular-session close. Extended-hours trading is thin: moves on small volume can reverse at the open.

paragraphs.speaker: Operator
paragraphs.text: Greetings, and welcome to the Microsoft Fiscal Year 2027 First Quarter earnings conference call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. A question-and-answer session will follow the formal presentation. If anyone should require Operator assistance, please press star zero on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. It is now my pleasure to introduce Jonathan Neilson, Vice President of Investor Relations.

paragraphs.speaker: Jonathan Neilson
paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining us today. On the call with me are Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Amy Hood, Chief Financial Officer, Alice Jolla, Chief Accounting Officer, and Brian DeFoe, Deputy General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. On the Microsoft Investor Relations website, you can find our earnings press release and financial summary slide deck, which is intended to supplement our prepared remarks during today's call and provides the reconciliation of differences between GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures. More detailed Outlook slides will be available on the Microsoft Investor Relations website when we provide Outlook commentary on today's call. On this call, we will discuss certain non-GAAP items. The non-GAAP financial measures provided should not be considered as a substitute for or superior to the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.

paragraphs.speaker: Jonathan Neilson
paragraphs.text: They are included as additional clarifying items to aid investors in further understanding the company's first quarter performance, in addition to the impact these items and events have on the financial results. All growth comparisons we make on the call today relate to the corresponding period of last year, unless otherwise noted. We will also provide growth rates in constant currency when available, as a framework for assessing how our underlying business performed, excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. Where growth rates are the same in constant currency, we will refer to the growth rate only. We will post our prepared remarks to our website immediately following the call until the complete transcript is available. Today's call is being webcast live and recorded. If you ask a question, it will be included in our live transmission, in the transcript, and in any future use of the recording.

paragraphs.speaker: Jonathan Neilson
paragraphs.text: You can replay the call and view the transcript on the Microsoft Investor Relations website. During this call, we will be making forward-looking statements, which are predictions, projections, or other statements about future events. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results could materially differ because of factors discussed in today's earnings press release, in the comments made during this conference call, and in the risk factors section of our Form 10-K, Forms 10-Q, and other reports and filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. We do not undertake any duty to update any forward-looking statements. With that, I'll turn the call over to Satya.

paragraphs.speaker: Satya Nadella
paragraphs.text: Thank you very much, Jonathan. It was a fast start to our fiscal year. Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassed $63 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% year-over-year. We are focused on three things: designing AI to empower people, ensuring every organization has sovereignty over its own learning, and building trust with controls that ensure agent safety and security. Now let's talk about how we are making progress on those goals as we build the new tech stack, starting with Copilot. We announced our biggest update to Copilot to date this quarter, bringing together chat, co-work, autopilot, and code into one unified experience. It's one product experience across commercial and consumer and comes with all of Office built in. We think of Copilot as the new OS for work. Customers are increasingly turning to Copilot to get real work done. Automated tasks has nearly doubled since July.

paragraphs.speaker: Satya Nadella
paragraphs.text: Daily users are up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter and over 5x year-over-year. User satisfaction improved nearly 20% quarter-over-quarter to another all-time high, and 90% of Copilot queries use auto mode, which dynamically routes tasks across models optimizing for quality, speed, and cost. These improvements are translating into larger purchases. The number of customers with more than 50,000 Copilot seats increased over 8x year-over-year, including Capgemini, HCLTech, Hitachi Group, Truist Financial, and U.K. Revenue and Customs Department. Just last week, Volkswagen announced plans to deploy Copilot to more than 330,000 employees, one of the largest deployments to date in Europe. We're also seeing strong momentum with E7, which brings together Copilot, E5, Entra, and Agent 365. Thousands of customers in every industry have purchased the suite to date, including Amadeus, BlackRock, Fiserv, New South Wales Health Department, and ZEISS.

hits.speaker: Amy Hood
hits.text: Based on current rates, we expect FX to have no meaningful impact on total revenue, COGS, or operating expense growth, or on revenue growth in either segment. Starting with segment guidance. We expect revenue from Agents and Infra of $80.1 billion-$80.7 billion, or growth of 24%-25%. In commercial bookings, we expect healthy growth in our commercial sales motions, though results will be impacted by the significant Azure commitments signed in the prior year. Timing related to significant Azure commitments like these will result in material volatility in bookings, making quarterly growth rates less indicative of underlying sales execution.

hits.speaker: Amy Hood
hits.text: In Dynamics 365, we expect revenue growth to be in the low teens, relatively stable quarter-over-quarter, driven by continued growth in ERP, although impacted by the bookings trends noted earlier. For Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $40.95 billion-$41.25 billion or growth of 33%-34%. In Azure, we expect revenue growth of approximately 45% in constant currency, we remain focused on delivering efficiencies that help us bridge the gaps we see as customer demand continues to exceed supply. Even with the strong close to Q4, we continue to expect H1 growth to accelerate. As a reminder, year-over-year Azure growth rates can vary quarter to quarter based on capacity, timing, and contract mix.

hits.speaker: Satya Nadella
hits.text: The number of Azure OpenAI apps running on Azure databases and Azure app services more than doubled year-over-year driving significant growth and adoption across SQL Hyperscale and Cosmos DB. Now on to AI platform and tools, as we shared last week we are thrilled OpenAI has made a new large Azure commitment. Through our strategic partnership we continue to benefit mutually from each other's growth and with OpenAI's APIs exclusively running on Azure customers can count on us to get access to the world's leading models and OpenAI has a lot more coming soon, so stay tuned.
